title: Enterprise Console Analytics walkthrough - usage & cost breakdown
next_steps: Lena to send tailored pricing and committed capacity options by 2025-04-13
Miguel to share a short runbook and console screenshots focused on per-route dashboards
Customer to provide sample traffic profile CSV for an initial cost estimate by 2025-04-15
action_items: Lena: Prepare pricing + dedicated capacity scenarios (due 2025-04-13)
Miguel: Export per-route dashboard sample and notes on tagging config (due 2025-04-12)
Devon: Share internal reqs for data residency and KMS integration (due 2025-04-15)
header: Date: 2025-04-10 | Time: 14:30 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Miguel Santos (Redwood SE), Aaron Cho (Redwood), Sasha Nguyen (Arbor), Devon Clarke (Arbor), Priya Patel (Arbor)
summary: Redwood presented the Console analytics and per-route dashboards with emphasis on cost breakdowns and policy-based routing. Customer asked about tagging, KMS, and how to map routes to billing lines. SE demoed the Optimize recommendations and a live per-route cost drilldown. Agreed next steps: pricing scenarios, sample traffic for cost modelling, and a short runbook for onboarding dedicated capacity.
transcript:
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll hand off to Miguel for the console deep-dive in about a minute. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Sasha: Hi Sasha here, also Priya and Devon are on from our side.
[00:12] Devon: hey, thanks, we're excited — we want to see cost visibility mostly.
[00:21] Miguel: Cool, so agenda for 30-40 minutes — console overview, per-route dashboards, cost breakdown by token and route, then optimize suggestions, then q&a.
[00:33] Miguel: (screen share) ok uh, this is the Console home, top left you can see per-route throughput, per-model breakdown, and a quick cost estimate, sometimes the automated caption shows "Redwood Optimaeyes" which is our Optimize module, ignore the auto-sub.
[00:50] Sasha: Quick question: can we map a route to an internal billing center? we have a lot of microservices that call the API.
[00:59] Miguel: Yes, you can tag routes, and tags show up in the per-route dashboard and the cost export. We'll demo how to tag and how it rolls up to a billing csv.
[01:12] Lena: I'll note that tagging is key for dedicated too — it lets us apply committed capacity across teams.
[01:25] Devon: Also want to understand prefix caching impact, like when we use KV cache — is that accounted for in token savings?
[01:37] Miguel: Yep, KV cache and prefix caching stats show under "Cache hits" and adjust the per-token billed estimate. The UI sometimes mislabels K V cache in the transcript export, haha.
[01:50] Miguel: (navigates) here is per-route dashboard for "patient-summarization" route — you can switch timeframe and see latency P50/P90, tokens-in/tokens-out, cost per 1k requests.
[02:05] Miguel: Note the breakdown: model compute cost, token cost, and infra overhead. Infra overhead is where dedicated reserved capacity pricing shows up differently.
[02:18] Priya: For security, we need to know where audit logs live and if console access can be restricted by role.
[02:27] Lena: We support RBAC with team-based roles, plus audit logs delivered to your S3 or SIEM, and KMS/HSM integrations for key control.
[02:40] Priya: Good. Also can you redact PHI before logs land in S3?
[02:46] Miguel: We have configurable redaction hooks and can integrate with your DLP pipeline. We'll send the security pack after this call.
[02:55] Sasha: Back to costs — if we route to a cheaper model for non-critical latency tolerant calls, can we see estimated savings?
[03:05] Miguel: Yep — in Optimize there's a compare view: you can pick model variants and see delta in cost and expected latency. For example, switching from base-llama-70b to a quantized variant shows storage and per-token compute savings. Expect the UI to show a projected monthly savings line.
[03:22] Devon: Does that projection include batching or is that separate?
[03:27] Miguel: Projections include default batching assumptions; you can customize the batch window and it recomputes the savings. Remember batching has latency trade-offs.
[03:40] Aaron: (interject) just to flag, customers often underestimate tail latency impact — we show P99 here too.
[03:47] Sasha: Can we export a CSV broken down by team, route, model and day?
[03:52] Miguel: Yes — export button -> choose dimensions: team, route, model, day — then we'll email you a link.
[04:05] Miguel: Now I want to demo the per-request cost drilldown — clicking a single route opens a waterfall with token counts by role (system/user/assistant), compute cost, and any cache credits.
[04:21] Miguel: (typing) here's a live example, you can see one request where prefix cache reduced 60% of tokens. The estimated cost peppered into the bottom is around $0.003 per request for this route.
[04:35] Devon: That seems low, is that for short prompts?
[04:39] Miguel: Yes it's for short prompts with strong prefix cache. For longer contexts numbers rise proportionally.
[04:46] (background noise)
[05:05] Sasha: Walk me through how routing policies appear in the console — for instance, can we have a fallback if dedicated capacity is saturated?
[05:13] Miguel: Absolutely — routing policy UI lets you create policies: prefer dedicated, fallback to hosted or a cheaper region. We show scoped metrics that indicate how often fallbacks occurred and the cost delta when they trigger.
[05:29] Miguel: Example: policy applied to "triage-bot" route — shows 3 fallback events last week; you can click the event to see the affected requests.
[05:40] Priya: About data residency — can we keep logs and model blobs in our VPC?
[05:46] Lena: For Private deployments we can do VPC and on-prem options. Model artifacts and logs can be kept in your region and hooked to your KMS. We'll include options in the security docs.
[05:57] Sasha: Any AD/SSO options?
[06:00] Aaron: Yes, SAML / OIDC single sign-on supported, you can map groups to Redwood roles.
[06:08] Miguel: (navigating) now the mid-section — usage analytics page, you can see anomaly detection for sudden token spikes and alerts tied to thresholds.
[06:20] Sasha: That's important — we had one week where a bad prompt multiplied token usage by 10x.
[06:27] Miguel: You'll get alerting, and we offer a throttling policy to cap spend automatically.
[06:36] Devon: How accurate are the cost attributions? sometimes cloud bills have surprises.
[06:41] Miguel: The console shows billed-estimate vs reconciled usage. We add an "expected variance" number and note known delta drivers — like network egress or third-party infra. We recommend a short pilot to reconcile.
[06:57] Sasha: Ok demo the Optimize recommendations — what does it surface?
[07:02] Miguel: Optimize runs evals across your prompt set — suggests batching, quantization levels, and model variants. It ties each suggestion to expected token or compute savings and a risk score.
[07:15] Miguel: Example suggestion: quantize to int8 on non-critical routes — estimated 40% compute savings, risk low but may increase latency a hair. The transcript auto-sub sometimes shows "quantizashun" which is a funny transcript artifact.
[07:30] Priya: Do we get a changelog or snapshot of model versions used for audit?
[07:36] Lena: Yes, rollouts and model pins create immutable snapshots and we keep a version history available in the console UI and logs.
[07:46] Miguel: (scrolling) here's the "cost per team" view — you can set budgets and get email alerts when a team is nearing spend thresholds.
[07:58] Sasha: Can budgets trigger automated routing changes to cheaper models?
[08:03] Miguel: Not directly out-of-the-box today, but we have a policy hook event you can subscribe to and then an automation layer can update routing. It's on the roadmap to make it first-class.
[08:16] Devon: For dedicated capacity, how granular are the autoscale policies?
[08:21] Miguel: You can configure min/max GPU pools, burst capacity, and time-of-day autoscaling. We show projected spend curves under different autoscale settings.
[08:33] Sasha: Do you have dashboards for P&L per customer route? like show revenue impact?
[08:40] Lena: We currently focus on cost; some customers export to their internal finance tools for P&L. We do provide exported CSVs that map route->cost->tag which helps build that view.
[08:53] Miguel: (minor pause) now I'm going to pull up a real customer example (redacted) to show how they tracked per-route cost over a quarter.
[09:05] Miguel: (scrolling) note here the spike corresponded to a model rollout where the fallback triggered to hosted, we annotated it in the timeline.
[09:17] Sasha: Seeing the annotation is really helpful for ops.
[09:22] Miguel: (typing) shared a link to a sample spreadsheet: https://redwood.example/samples/route-costs.csv (note: demo links are placeholders).
[09:35] Devon: On the topic of export, can we schedule daily extracts to an S3 bucket?
[09:40] Miguel: Yes — scheduled exports can push to S3 with prefixing by team/route.
[09:50] Priya: For compliance review we'll need SOC2 reports and also a data flow diagram.
[09:57] Lena: We'll attach SOC2 and an architecture diagram in the security bundle.
[10:05] (10m mark)
[10:10] Miguel: I'm going to flip to a quick runthrough of the tagging best-practices — tag at the route and API-key level, and enforce via policy.
[10:24] Miguel: (typing) example tags: team:clinical, env:prod, billing_center:CH-12. You can then filter dashboards by those tags.
[10:36] Sasha: If we have 200 routes how usable is the UI?
[10:41] Miguel: We have search, saved filters, and you can bulk-apply tagging rules via API. We'll include sample scripts.
[10:50] Aaron: Customers with scale usually automate tag enforcement in CI.
[10:55] Devon: How do we handle per-request metadata, like patient id? we can't store PHI in logs.
[11:03] Miguel: We support token redaction and hashing of identifiers before they make it to logs; transforms are configurable.
[11:12] Sasha: Now show us the ROI calc for moving 30% of calls to a quantized cheaper model.
[11:18] Miguel: (switch) here's a compare: current 100k calls/month -> projected savings $4,200/mo with 30% migration, and estimated change in latency +8ms average.
[11:33] Devon: What's the upfront work to pilot?
[11:36] Lena: Typically 2-4 weeks: set up tagging & exports, run Optimize on your sampled traffic, pilot 1-2 routes, then measure.
[11:48] Sasha: Who will support the pilot?
[11:51] Lena: We'll allocate an AE and an SE for onboarding; Miguel will be primary SE.
[11:58] Priya: Any additional security checks for pilot?
[12:01] Miguel: For pilot we can do scoped VPC peering and limited data retention; full Private deployment takes extra time but is doable.
[12:10] (laughter)
[12:18] Miguel: Quick detour — here's the per-token charge breakdown, note the console shows 'tokenized' and sometimes mislabels roles as "assistang" but the numbers are right.
[12:31] Miguel: Another feature: route-level seals that mark traffic as sensitive, preventing certain exports unless cleared.
[12:40] Priya: We'll use that for PHI traffic.
[12:44] Sasha: Can we run an isolated benchmark of latency from our region?
[12:49] Miguel: Yes, we can run a latency bench from your VPC or your region endpoints; we'll include it in the pilot scope.
[12:59] Devon: Do you have examples of customers reducing cost by caching?
[13:03] Miguel: Yes — one customer reduced token spend 35% by prefix caching and smarter prompts; we redacted their name but will share a case study link.
[13:15] Aaron: Sharing that doc after the call.
[13:22] Sasha: A question on billing frequency — monthly or daily usage invoicing?
[13:27] Lena: Standard is monthly, but we can do daily exports for reconciliation.
[13:34] Miguel: (moving on) now I'm going to show how to create a routing policy in the console — step 1: create a new policy, step 2: add conditions by header, path, or tag, step 3: set priority and fallback.
[13:51] Miguel: (typing) I'm creating a sample rule for "low-priority-summary" to prefer cheaper model and fallback to hosted.
[14:04] Sasha: Could routing be based on runtime metrics like P99 over last 10m?
[14:10] Miguel: We support metric-based triggers for autoscaling and some event-based reroutes; full dynamic rerouting by real-time P99 is on the near-term roadmap.
[14:24] Devon: For the pilot, we'd like the console to send Slack alerts on budget thresholds.
[14:29] Miguel: That's supported — webhook to Slack or webhook to your incident management.
[14:36] (15m mark)
[14:44] Sasha: Any particular gotchas you recommend we watch for during onboarding?
[14:48] Miguel: Two things — tagging hygiene and prompt engineering to reduce tokens. Also watch for hidden costs like third-party embeddings or long-term KV storage.
[14:58] Priya: On KMS — we need Bring Your Own Key; is that supported?
[15:02] Lena: Yes, BYOK through most major KMS providers; we'll document key rotation and access.
[15:12] Miguel: (scroll) moving on, here are alerting templates and example slack messages.
[15:20] Devon: We might want a whitelist of routes that never go to cheaper models — can we enforce that?
[15:26] Miguel: Yes, route-level policy can be marked "never downgrade" and overrides other policies.
[15:33] Sasha: The per-route latency P99 spike info — can that be correlated to specific model versions?
[15:38] Miguel: We store model version metadata per request so you can correlate.
[15:44] Aaron: (note) keeping good metadata on requests is essential for triage.
[15:50] Miguel: (demo pause) Now I'll show an example of the 'billing insights' card, it summarizes costs by model family and by team.
[16:02] Miguel: It also surfaces 'unusual spend' and suggests a root-cause link to recent rollouts or traffic changes.
[16:12] Sasha: If we see unusual spend, what's the fastest way to remediate?
[16:17] Miguel: You can temporary throttle a route, change policy to cheaper model, or revoke keys. The console exposes those controls.
[16:27] Devon: Do you keep an immutable event log for all policy changes?
[16:31] Lena: Yes — all changes are auditable with who/when and the diff.
[16:38] Miguel: (switch) I'm going to share a small snippet of the Optimize report — it will display suggestion, expected savings, confidence score and rollout steps.
[16:50] Miguel: For each suggestion we create a safe rollout recipe: canary X% -> monitor -> increase.
[16:58] Sasha: Good. We'll probably pilot with canary to 5% initially.
[17:04] Miguel: Sounds reasonable.
[17:10] (17m mark)
[17:17] Priya: About exporting logs to our SIEM — what format?
[17:21] Miguel: JSONL with schemas for request and response, includes hashed identifiers when configured.
[17:30] Devon: Are there sampling settings? we don't need full payloads.
[17:34] Miguel: Yes, you can set sampling ratios per route and set sampling for error traces only.
[17:44] Sasha: For the cost model, do you charge for cached tokens?
[17:49] Miguel: We only charge for tokens served that are not satisfied by cache credits; the console shows cache credits used and billing offsets.
[17:58] Miguel: (note) sometimes the auto-transcript shows model names with slight typos like "base llama" as "bass lama" but ignore these.
[18:08] Devon: Can we get a sample billing export for our current traffic pattern?
[18:13] Miguel: Yes — please send the traffic sample CSV and we'll run a modeled export.
[18:21] Sasha: Sending that after the call.
[18:24] Miguel: Ok next demo: per-route SLA monitoring — set SLOs and get alerted if route violates.
[18:34] Miguel: Example: patient-summarization SLO P95 < 300ms; we show a heatmap of violations.
[18:44] Priya: How granular are traces? can we see which kernel or GPU was used?
[18:50] Miguel: We log backend host and GPU type for each request in traces for Dedicated; in Hosted we show the region and model variant.
[19:00] Devon: That helps with perf debugging.
[19:06] Miguel: (moving on) I'm going to share the onboarding runbook link: https://redwood.example/onboarding/runbook (placeholder).
[19:18] Sasha: Perfect.
[19:22] Miguel: (19m mark) now Q&A from the team?
[19:26] Devon: Is the per-route cost computed daily?
[19:30] Miguel: Cost estimates update in near real-time; definitive reconciled numbers are nightly.
[19:40] Priya: For audit purposes we need a monthly immutable snapshot.
[19:45] Lena: We can create monthly snapshots and export them to your archive bucket.
[19:52] Miguel: (demoing) now the Optimize 'what-if' slider — you can simulate migrations and it graphically shows cost curves.
[20:05] Miguel: This helps answer "move 20% traffic to quantized model" scenario.
[20:12] Sasha: How do we validate output quality post-migration?
[20:18] Miguel: Optimize includes evaluation hooks; you can run a prompt set against both models and compute metrics like ROUGE/BLEU or custom eval scripts.
[20:29] Sasha: Great.
[20:32] Miguel: (21m mark) Some housekeeping: we'll follow up with the security bundle and the pricing scenarios.
[20:41] Sasha: Timeline question — if we sign a dedicated deal, how soon can we be live?
[20:46] Lena: For Dedicated typically 6-8 weeks after contract; Private on-prem longer. Pilot can be immediate in hosted.
[20:56] Devon: Ok.
[21:00] Miguel: (navigating) lastly, here's the cost anomaly explorer — shows sudden spikes and suggests root causes by correlating deployments and model changes.
[21:12] Miguel: You can then create a ticket directly from the UI with the relevant logs attached.
[21:20] Sasha: That could shave a lot of MTTR.
[21:26] Priya: Are there retention controls for logs per legal requirement?
[21:31] Miguel: Retention policies per tag/route, and you can set legal hold exceptions.
[21:39] Devon: For the pilot, can we restrict logs to 30 days?
[21:43] Lena: Yes — that's configurable.
[21:48] Miguel: (pause) now I'll show the API for pulling usage programmatically — it's a REST endpoint that returns JSON with dimensions you select.
[22:00] Miguel: Example call: GET /v1/usage?route=patient-summary&period=2025-03. We'll share sample curl.
[22:12] Sasha: We'll want that for our finance ingestion.
[22:16] Miguel: We'll send sample code in Python and Golang.
[22:23] (23m mark)
[22:28] Devon: Do you support custom price mapping for internal chargebacks?
[22:32] Miguel: You can upload price multipliers in the console and compute internal chargeback reports.
[22:40] Sasha: Nice.
[22:44] Miguel: (demo) here's a saved report configuration that runs weekly and posts to S3.
[22:53] Priya: For security review, we'll need a mapping of data at rest vs in transit.
[22:58] Lena: Included in the security bundle.
[23:05] Miguel: (24m mark) starting to wind down, any final deep technical things we should cover?
[23:13] Devon: Just one — hardware specifics for Dedicated: what GPU types and how do you map models to GPUs?
[23:20] Miguel: We publish the supported GPU SKUs and scoring matrix; the runtime chooses kernels and may move a model to a different VM class depending on quantization. We'll share the matrix.
[23:34] Sasha: Are there options for hotter/higher-io networks?
[23:38] Miguel: Yes, express network and colocated regions are available as add-ons.
[23:44] Miguel: (24m mark) ok recap time.
[23:50] Lena: Recap: 1) Miguel to share per-route dashboard screenshots and tagging best practices. 2) Lena to send pricing scenarios for hosted vs dedicated and committed capacity. 3) Customer to send sample traffic CSV. 4) Redwood to share security bundle and SOC2.
[24:12] Sasha: That aligns.
[24:18] Miguel: Anything else?
[24:22] Priya: We'll schedule a follow-up security call next week.
[24:26] Devon: We'll try to get the traffic CSV to you by Wednesday.
[24:31] Miguel: Great.
[24:35] (closing)
[24:40] Lena: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and links.
[24:44] Sasha: Thank you.
[24:47] (end of recording)
